I am an old woman now, 71 years, but this land is mine and I have farmed it since I was young. Kilimanjaro soil is still good but not like before, so I put manure from my cows and goats on the maize plot every season — it costs me nothing but the labor of my grandchildren to carry it. I will buy some CAN for top-dressing if the price at the Moshi agro-dealer is not too high this year, but only a little because six hectares is a big plot and fertilizer is expensive. I plant the improved maize seed I bought last season because my neighbor's harvest was better than mine when she used it, and I intercrop with beans like I always do; for such a big plot I cannot manage alone at my age, so my sons and their wives help and I hire some young men from the village for weeding and harvest.
